column3: The lower construction gives 3^ell but a proof needs an upper bound for every graph with ell edges and every family of infinite permutations; optimizing a fixed finite graph misses that quantifier. No uniform compression to 3 choices per edge established.

Nielsen orbit connectivity must hold for every finite group with only one spare generator. The primary bounds d(G)+mu(G) and solvable cases do not close the gap to d(G)+1 for arbitrary nonsolvable groups; park structural group program.

The orientable double-cover strategy only yields c(g-1). The primary conclusion explicitly says other orientable branched covers factor through that cover, so improving the cover alone cannot establish c(floor(g/2)) for all genera.

A greedy character-sum construction might add a point with square distances while excluding all old lines and circles, but it needs a uniform finite-field estimate for every sufficiently large prime, not isolated computed primes. General-position and successor checks remain unaudited; standard construction risk precludes investment.

Primary Conjecture 2 names Lemmas 2 and 3, versus Lemmas 1 and 2 in the literal record. Need the actual two formulas and a prime-power/CRT upper bound for all n; the source's n<=307 clique enumeration is not a universal proof and renumbering earns no credit.

The integral rhombus (0,0),(8,0),(4,3),(4,-3) is a complete literal counterexample: six integral distances, no collinear triple, noncyclic. This drops the minimum-diameter motivation surrounding primary Theorem 1; a wording/scope correction is excluded from discovery credit.

Need show every diameter minimizer on every n>=9 has n-1 collinear points, not merely exhibit such sets. Primary Theorem 3 covers 9<=n<=122; efficient near-collinear constructions give upper bounds only and do not exclude alternative minimizers.

Entropy inequality quantifies over all auxiliary joint laws. Independent U,V and restricted input-bias cases in the primary passage cannot remove dependence or the remaining bias interval. A binary numerical optimizer would not certify all cardinalities or prior resolution.

Nonuniform subdivision lengths are the obstruction: subdividing further can reduce cop number, so the primary uniform two-cop construction is not monotone in the needed direction. Full scope implies Meyniel's conjecture; park deep program.

Packing equality for all minors must force normality of the whole Rees semigroup, not just integrality of the covering polyhedron. Primary Theorem 2.9 gives integrality and Conjecture 2.12 still asks normality; no Hilbert-basis certificate uniform in clutters.

Non-r.e. order theory does not imply non-r.e. equational theory. Primary Theorem 5 treats freely generated finite partial webs, whereas Conjecture 3 includes every effective graph model; extending the computability obstruction is a structural program.

Primary concluding passage says Liu and Pelsmajer claim to have verified both conjectures. Must inspect that successor before any proof investment. Bounded curvature defects alone do not supply a uniform n_t with domination at most n/4.

Literal conditioning on history needs a filtration audit: if H_t already reveals R(t), conditional expectation equals R(t) tautologically. The real source decoder variables and exposure process must be checked before applying Azuma/Wormald; a notation tautology is not eligible discovery.

Need a linear space of matrices of dimension min nu_i avoiding all nonzero ranks below delta for every field q and Ferrers shape. Generic coefficients over a large extension do not give the required base-field construction; isolated small codes are instances only.

Equality needs a universal Ramsey transition upper bound matching the recursively constructed lower family. Infinitely many nice s in the source do not cover all s; no finite certificate can replace a structural recurrence or complete extremal argument.

Need upper-bound every three-coloring's prescribed triples by g(s), including nonrecursive colorings. The source's nice-s results leave the same global gap; this is stronger than the paired transition conjecture and cannot be counted as a separate routine consequence.

Must read the exact likelihood monomial exponents and rank/nonnegative/normalization feasible variety before a global comparison. Primary Conjecture 13 displays the candidate; Hessian or symmetric subfamily stationarity would not certify every feasible P or boundary degeneration.

A universal 1.25 speedup upper bound is a stable-set polytope dilation statement for all K,N enhanced conflict graphs. The source's 2xN discussion and five-hole lower obstruction do not prove the general upper inclusion; tiny switch exceptions would be domain corrections only.

Need exact discrete equations and energy weights before eliminating variables at fixed N. Continuation of one feasible branch does not prove the global minimum vanishes as R grows, nor existence for every R. No symbolic asymptotic certificate executed.

Need exact generator-degree lower and upper bounds in the characteristic-zero graph invariant ring for every n>=4. Hilbert series or one separating invariant is insufficient to certify an indecomposable generator and generation in all degrees; finite n computations are instances.

Uniqueness of the ground-energy minimizing alpha requires global spectral control for every positive k. The primary source already cites Pan-Kwek and Aramaki cases; those proofs and subsequent refinements must be checked. Local nondegeneracy does not prove uniqueness.

Primary Theorem 2.9 supplies phi>=t(g)delta_0+sum 2i(g-i)/g delta_i, with explicit positive t(g), and says it proves Conjecture 2.6. This directly supplies the requested genus-dependent positive coefficient. No independent whole proof/dependency audit claimed; discovery credit is already blocked by the source theorem.

Need distinguish exact identity from correct order and homomorphism from injective density. The primary balanced blowup conjecture needs the all-graph lower bound, while random graphs supply the comparison upper bound; finite-size density rounding is not eligible refutation.

Record and primary introductory wording both claim equality and a coloring-derived upper bound. The biclique-completeness step in that upper bound is invalid for a general coloring; intended lower-bound scope requires independent successor reading. C5 has chromatic number 3 but needs three bicliques to partition five edges, disproving literal equality routinely. Does not resolve intended lower-bound conjecture or establish novelty.

Need disjoint 2-plexes exhausting every even-order square, or leaving one transversal for odd order. Finding a single duplex does not iterate through a Latin square after removal; odd case includes Ryser. Source soluble-group cases do not cover all squares.

Merging species embeds one-species eigenvalues but does not exclude additional eigenvalues nearer zero in the full nonsymmetric generator. Need an all-sector spectral exclusion, not diagonalizing finitely many sectors or assuming Bethe completeness.

Need a single k forbidding all additive k-by-k square grids, with unbounded integer heights. Primary passage permits 3-by-k grids for every k; finite searches cannot control heights, and Bombieri-Lang-based uniformity would be a conditional result only.

Need orbit classification or alphabet-extension recurrence for every odd prime D, not just D=3. Primary discussion explicitly requires new extension functions for all increments below D; computing coefficients cannot prove the rational EGF degree bound.

From reaching t pebbles at any one vertex one cannot reserve them while making the other targets. Primary Lemma 3.2 needs a controlled pebble cost at each induction step; known trees/cycles/cubes are instances and do not supply the universal cost inequality.

Need simultaneous universal constants C<=10 and alpha in [0.18,0.21) across all minimum degrees. Alteration bounds with a logarithmic loss or the primary alpha=0.13 small-degree range fail that scope; finite graph scans cannot establish the universal claim.

Uniform linear curvature in number of facets needs control independent of dimension, not average curvature across cells. Primary continuous d-step equivalence suggests seeking a superlinear central path family; later tropical/central-path constructions require actual successor inspection before any new claim.

Primary introduction proves the stronger chi(D)<=h(D) via a realization with a clique subdivision, and h(D)<=H(D). Theorems 4.1 and 3.5 are identified there; their formal/dependency audit is not performed, but the exact target is already announced as settled by its own source.

Virtualization of crossings and choosing over/under resolutions are different operations. Need the exact primary definition of tr(S) before using chord deletion parity; the classical-shadow evenness proof alone does not cover all virtual shadows.

Deleting a bounded number of discriminant prime factors still leaves a uniform height/discriminant problem over all elliptic curves. No bounded-height enumeration controls J and C for an entire number field; source relates it to prime-depleted ABC, so park arithmetic program.

Need weighted hook identity for every connected d-complete poset, not q=t or shapes/shifted shapes/rooted trees proved in source Propositions 4.5-4.6. General d-complete/Macdonald successors must be inspected; specialization or routine hook adaptation earns no credit.

Need feedback arc set <=half the missing pairs in every 3-free digraph. Local edge deletion can destroy the invariant accounting; the primary 0.88 and 1 bounds do not give 0.5. Small exact digraph tests would not establish the all-size result.

Literal statement omits the relation m=floor(n^alpha) and admissible probability regime from the random-intersection model. Need restore source assumptions before threshold coupling; a degenerate m or p>1 refutation would be only a domain correction, excluded from credit.

Normal core is contained in N but semisparsity is not visibly hereditary under arbitrary subgroup inclusion. Need exact distinguished-generator/intersection conditions and a finite regular-cover theorem; the source finite group search cannot prove core semisparsity for all W.

Source uses boundary regular critical graphs, so degree conventions and f_3(n) must be fixed before Euler counting. Force balance alone can permit cycles and does not bound all interior vertices; degree-three extremal comparisons need an actual geometric reduction.

The two complementary tuple-degree inequalities give density and fractional matching information, but an integral perfect matching must avoid conflicts in every part simultaneously. Hall on a graph of tuples does not ensure coordinate-disjointness; source fractional theorem is not the required integral result.

Record uses every point set whereas blocking-number minima in the source need quantifier reconciliation. Midpoint superlinearity does not transfer: arbitrary blockers can lie at unequal ratios. An all-configuration incidence bound with fixed collinearity cap is still needed.

Need prove 5-chromatic graphs form a vanishing fraction in the fixed-genus distribution. Linear K4 copies prove the lower bound 4 and large facewidth gives 5-colorability, but neither eliminates global 5-color obstructions; enumeration needs uniform asymptotic control.

Need a superlinear lower bound for the smallest possible blocker set across all general-position configurations. Shared blockers on many segments defeat pair counting; midpoint bounds only constrain a chosen construction. No uniform incidence mechanism closes the linear-to-superlinear gap.

Both ranges demand sharp size and uniqueness of equality families, including near n=2k. Large-n compression bounds do not yield the exact threshold or equality classification; missing k>=r conventions are a scope check, not a new result.

Primary triple (8,9,15) gives only f(3)<=14; full equality requires rule out discrepancy drops below 14 for every coprime triple. Repeating source search through largest generator 200 gives no universal certificate; exact g_j convention and parametric Apéry analysis needed.

Primary Observation 3 reverses the shuffling poset, and symmetrizing upward/downward weights gives an existing symmetric function, but neither proves the particular upward algorithm returns one. Literal 31-i is an example for N=32; changing to N-1-i is a wording fix, not credit.

The source calls this a meta-conjecture for choosing a family, not an assertion for arbitrary homology and arbitrary family. F=ALL is automatic; arbitrary F fails in elementary classifying-space examples. Such a generic counterexample would correct packaging rather than resolve Farrell-Jones/Baum-Connes.

Primary Theorem 1.4 gives concentration at each positive strict maximum and subsequent theorems impose conditions excluding concentration elsewhere. Must compare H1, degeneracies and boundary hypotheses exactly; source already advertises a resolution under mild assumptions, so no claim from its abstract alone.

A support graph with a vertex of larger degree would need exact positive rational weights, every subtour cut inequality, and enough independent tight constraints to certify extremality. Degree-only examples or numeric LP vertices are insufficient; no full-scope certificate located or executed.

Rapidly growing finite ranks of related groups do not imply a fixed H^i(J_n^s) is infinitely generated. Need infinitely many independent classes surviving in that one subgroup in each indicated degree; source Johnson images give finite-rank information only.
